scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf's red exactly: the fire must never stay out for long; a smoulder must relight in open grass, so a map that stays fireless for good contradicts it
scenarios.text: On a new Pyrelands colony the line of fire crosses the plain on the first day and burns itself out. From the third day to the end of the second week there is not a single flame anywhere on the map, and nothing ever relights.

scenarios.expect: reject: ordinary crops on deep ash must still benefit from water, the watered strip growing clearly faster; equal growth is the leaf's red
scenarios.text: I planted two rows of rice on the grey ash on the same day, one right along an irrigation ditch and one a few tiles away on dry ash. After five days both rows are at exactly the same growth, the water made no difference at all.

scenarios.expect: reject: black rain must add to the fresh-burn bonus, not wipe it; a rained-on fresh scar doing no better than wet old ash is the leaf's red
scenarios.text: I sowed corn on a scar the fire had just crossed, then black rain fell on it for half a day. Afterwards that corn grew no better than corn on long-burned ash under the same rain, as if the rain had rinsed the fresh-burn boost away.

scenarios.expect: reject: scorch-fruit must come up only in freshly burned ground, never on unburned ground, and must not read as an ordinary wild bush
scenarios.text: Scorch-fruit bushes are dotted across stretches of grass that no fire has ever touched, growing up like any other wild shrub far from the burn.

scenarios.expect: reject: ordinary rain must never fall on a Pyrelands map; its only wet weather is black rain
scenarios.text: Halfway through summer on my Pyrelands map an ordinary blue-grey rain shower rolls in and drizzles over the colony for a few hours.

scenarios.expect: reject: a shovelled sand cell must turn to gravel and be finite; a cell that stays sand and can be dug forever is the leaf's red
scenarios.text: My colonist shovels a patch of Pyrelands sand, gets the glass sand, and the tile is still sand afterwards; I keep ordering the same tile dug and it pays out every time.

scenarios.expect: reject: a flamefang bite must put flamefang venom on the health tab that worsens over hours; a plain wound only is the leaf's red
scenarios.text: A flamefang bites my colonist twice. Her health tab shows only two bite wounds, with no venom or other condition listed, and nothing gets worse over the next hours.

scenarios.expect: accept: the beast must be a giant far larger than other animals and give a readable warmth status nearby that ends when the colonist leaves
scenarios.text: The furnace-beast towers over every other animal on the map, dwarfing even the biggest grazers. When my colonist stands in the open beside it she gets a warmth status in her needs, and the status goes away once she walks off.

scenarios.expect: accept: the ashwallow must show a burrowed status and dive as the front arrives, and surface unharmed after it passes
scenarios.text: As the fire front reaches an ashwallow it shows a burrowed status and disappears into the ground; once the flames have moved past, it comes back up with full health and not a single burn.

scenarios.expect: accept: the fire-hawk must pick up a burning twig at the fire and start a new fire where it drops it, ahead of the blaze
scenarios.text: A fire-hawk swoops down to the blaze, flies off carrying a burning twig, and drops it in the grass well ahead of the fire; a new fire starts there before the main blaze gets anywhere near.

scenarios.expect: accept: black rain must fall visibly dark, not blue-grey, and put fires out
scenarios.text: When black rain comes it falls in visibly dark, sooty streaks unlike any normal rain, and the grass fires burning on the map go out under it.

scenarios.expect: accept: a burned ember-grass patch must visibly re-green within a few days and be largely green within about a week, neither instantly green nor black for a season
scenarios.text: A patch of ember grass burns black. A few days later green shoots are clearly coming through the scar, and by the end of the week most of the patch is green again.

scenarios.expect: accept: the biome description must say the savanna was genetically engineered and has burned for millennia
scenarios.text: Hovering the Pyrelands biome on the world map, the description explains that this grassland was genetically engineered long ago and has been burning for thousands of years.

scenarios.expect: accept: a colonist carrying the sprayer must foam a way through the live burn, pick the fruit in the scar and return unburned
scenarios.text: I send a colonist with the firefoam sprayer into a fire that is still burning to get the ripe scorch-fruit in its scar. He foams the flames out along his way in, picks the fruit and walks back out without a single burn.

scenarios.expect: reject: scorchfruit_born_of_fire says scorch-fruit comes up rapidly in the fresh scar right behind the front while the ground still smokes, and must not read as fruit that appears days after the fire; red lists fruit appearing only days after the front passed.
scenarios.text: The burn line crosses the grass and leaves a black, smoking scar. For the first two days the scar stays bare; on the third morning a crop of scorch-fruit comes up across it, ripens, a colonist picks it and eats it, and the leftover fruit rots within a few days.

scenarios.expect: reject: fresh_burn_compounds_with_black_rain says black rain adds to the burn bonus instead of washing it away, so a wet fresh scar must out-grow wet old ash; matching wet old ash is exactly its red (rain wipes the bonus).
scenarios.text: A colonist sows rice on ground the fire crossed this morning and on old ash nearby, and the fresh-burn rice pulls clearly ahead. Then black rain falls on both for half a day; from then on the fresh-burn rice grows at the same pace as the rained-on old-ash rice, and both outpace a dry patch.

scenarios.expect: reject: no_ordinary_rain (a does-not line) says ordinary rain never falls on a Pyrelands map and its only wet weather is black rain; any ordinary rain shower breaks it.
scenarios.text: Most weeks the sky turns between ash fall, cinderfall and dark black rain as expected. Once in late summer an ordinary grey-blue rain shower passes over the colony for a few hours, damping the grass fire before clearing.

scenarios.expect: reject: furnacebeast_warms says the furnace-beast is a giant, standing far larger than any other animal, and must not read as a beast the size of a muffalo; red includes an ordinary-sized beast.
scenarios.text: A furnace-beast wanders up to the colony; it is about the size of the muffalo grazing beside it. Colonists standing near it get a warmth status that goes when they walk away, the barn it shelters in runs clearly hotter than the empty one next door, and the grass it sleeps on catches after a while.

scenarios.expect: reject: flamefang_bite_carries_venom says the venom comes from a flamefang's bite and no other bite does; its false_pass is any bite applying the venom, and the control is a non-venomous predator leaving no venom.
scenarios.text: During a predator attack a flamefang bites one colonist and a wolf bites another. Both colonists' health tabs show a bite wound and flamefang venom that grows worse over the following hours until the doctor treats them.

scenarios.expect: reject: ash_ground_and_blowing_ash says a lot of ash blows across the ground like snow in any weather, and must not read as a clear sky with ash only on the ground; red includes no ash blowing in clear weather, and its false_pass is blowing ash that shows only during ash fall.
scenarios.text: On a fresh map the ground is almost all deep ash, with small soil pockets and richer ground by the water. When ash fall sets in, the map dims and thick ash flakes drift across it like snow and bank up in drifts; on clear days the sky is clean and nothing blows, only the grey ground shows.
